item.content:encoded:
Festive Rush Comes At A Cost 

India’s ecommerce sellers are heading into the festive rush with a growing cost burden. While Amazon India and Flipkart have cut commissions to attract more sellers, higher cancellation penalties, platform fees and logistics costs are denting their margins just as festive demand peaks. Meanwhile, subdued discretionary spending and rising logistics costs are adding to their woes. But what’s really happening? 

Flipkart’s Penalty Shot: Flipkart’s zero-commission push across fashion categories in July has nearly doubled seller onboarding. However, its new penalty structure charges sellers ₹30 for delayed dispatches and another ₹60 for cancelled orders, regardless of order value. This flat fee is hurting smaller sellers and low-value orders, taking the shine off its zero-commission model.

Amazon Plays Spoilsport, Too: The ecommerce giant has followed suit. It has revised its cancellation fee structure, linking charges to order value instead of slapping a flat fee. Amazon’s flat tier-based penalty for cancelled orders can go up to 10% of the order value for orders up to ₹10,000, falling to 8% for orders between ₹10,001 and ₹50,000, 5% for orders between ₹50,001 and ₹1 lakh, and 2% for orders above ₹1 lakh. An additional 18% GST applies to these charges.

Deliveries Turn Costlier: Rising logistics costs are also adding to the festive-season strain, with Amazon raising closing fees and Delhivery introducing a surcharge on D2C shipments. Flipkart is also considering a revision in seller fulfilment fees. Quick commerce is adding to the pressure, with frequent, smaller shipments increasing vehicle requirements and waiting times at distribution hubs.

Sellers In A Tight Corner: The shift to value-linked cancellation fees adds to the cost of doing business on marketplaces, particularly for those operating on thin margins. Sellers have also flagged the difficulty of contesting such charges, saying the process can be cumbersome even when they have evidence of timely dispatch. 

With penalties, surcharges and logistics costs piling up, here’s how ecommerce sellers are paying the price.

From The Editor’s Desk

WeWork India Q2 Profit Jumps 219%

  • WeWork India’s net profit surged 219% YoY to ₹20.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue rose 33.6% to ₹767.8 Cr. The company added a record 11,700 desks during the quarter.
  • Operational capacity grew 26.9% YoY to 1,45,300 desks across 85 centres in eight cities. Its member base rose 32.5% to 1,21,700, while occupancy stood at 83.7%.
  • Value-added services and digital revenue grew 38% to ₹108.8 Cr, outpacing core revenue growth. WeWork India also reported a net cash position of ₹23.1 Cr, compared with net debt of ₹310.5 Cr a year earlier.

 Baillie Gifford Funds Mark Down VerSe By Up To 80%

  • Two funds managed by Baillie Gifford slashed the value of their VerSe Innovation holdings by around 80% over different periods. One fund’s assessment implied a valuation of about $576 Mn, nearly 90% below its $5 Bn valuation in 2022.
  • VerSe Innovation, the parent of Dailyhunt and Josh, last raised $805 Mn in April 2022 at a reported $5 Bn valuation. The company has raised nearly $1.7 Bn from investors including Google, Microsoft and Peak XV Partners.
  • VerSe reported an 88% YoY rise in FY25 operating revenue to ₹1,930 Cr, while its EBITDA burn narrowed 20% to ₹738 Cr. However, the latest markdowns reflect investor concerns and do not establish a definitive company-wide valuation.

Practo Cofounder’s Cent Raises $15 Mn

  • Healthtech startup Cent raised $15 Mn in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. It also acquired AI-powered radiology platform Medsee to improve reporting workflows.
  • Founded by Practo cofounder Shashank ND and two other executives, Cent combines AI, radiology and biomarkers to screen asymptomatic patients for over 300 conditions, including cancer and cardiac disease.
  • Cent said it has completed 10,000 preventive whole-body scans across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR. It plans to use the fresh capital to expand its AI, engineering and clinical teams, and scale to 1 Cr scans by 2035.

Parsec Aerospace In Talks To Raise $10 Mn

  • Bengaluru-based Parsec Aerospace is in talks to raise around $10 Mn in a funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Lightspeed Venture Partners, sources told Inc42.
  • Founded by former Pixxel engineer Effy John, Parsec Aerospace is developing next-generation engines for aerospace applications. Incorporated in September 2025, the startup remains in stealth mode.
  • The funding talks come as Indian deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals in Q3 2026, nearly 2.8X the $105 Mn raised in the year-ago quarter. Recent investments include aerospace propulsion startup D-Propulse Aerospace’s ₹25 Cr fundraise.

 IndiaMART’s Q2 Snapshot

  • IndiaMART’s net profit rose 9.8% YoY to ₹90.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue grew 10% to ₹428.6 Cr. EBITDA fell 2% to ₹156 Cr, but margins improved 300 bps to 40%.
  • Customer collections increased 9% YoY to ₹443 Cr during the quarter. The B2B ecommerce platform recorded 2.7 Cr unique business enquiries, while its paying suppliers stood at 2.2 Lakh.
  • Annualised revenue per paying supplier rose 10% to around ₹72,000, supporting marketplace revenue growth. However, profit declined 47.3% sequentially from ₹172.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Protonas Is Making Hydrogen Power More Affordable

Backup power in India often means diesel generators. But these are costly to run, pollute the environment and have high upfront costs. To solve this, Protonas is redesigning PEM fuel cells to make hydrogen power viable where traditional batteries fall short.

A Cost-First Design: Founded in 2024, Protonas is building air-cooled proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells. This technology converts hydrogen and oxygen into electricity, with water as the only point-of-use byproduct. Its stack architecture uses fewer components and simpler cooling systems, which the startup claims can slash manufacturing and operating costs. 

Lighting Up India: Protonas is building systems for backup power, mobility and UAVs. Its 500W–2kW systems for telecom networks and critical infrastructure are designed to provide eight to 72 hours of backup during outages. The startup is also developing fuel-cell engines for three-wheelers, alongside systems aimed at extending drone flight times. 

Building In India: Backed by Transition VC, Protonas now plans to build its engineering and manufacturing operations in Bengaluru. Competing with the likes of Ballard Power Systems and Plug Power, it is now focused on developing affordable prototype systems for emerging markets. So, can Protonas make hydrogen fuel cells affordable and mainstream?

item.title: Exclusive: QwikBuild Raises $2.3 Mn To Expand Enterprise AI Platform
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Bengaluru-based enterprise AI startup QwikBuild has raised $2.3 Mn (around ₹22 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round led by Japanese…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based enterprise AI startup QwikBuild has raised $2.3 Mn (around ₹22 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round led by Japanese tech major Globalway, along with participation from Blume Ventures, DeVC, Marsshot and angel investors Lalit Keshre, founder of Groww, and Curefoods’ CEO Ankit Nagori.

The startup will use the fresh capital primarily to fuel its go-to-market (GTM) activities. This will include setting up a team in the US as well as expanding operations across South East Asia. 

Besides the investment, QwikBuild also announced that it is forming a joint venture (JV) with Globalway to enter Japan’s enterprise software market. Expected to become operational by the end of 2026, the JV will take QwikBuild’s platform to Globalway’s existing and prospective enterprise customers in Japan.

Founded in 2025 by ex-slice executive Pradeep Ayyagari, QwikBuild builds enterprise software and AI agents that can bring down the software development and deployment significantly. 

The startup claims to be serving more than 100 enterprises across India, Southeast Asia, the US and Dubai. It says that about 10-12% of its clients are large enterprises, while about 30% are smaller businesses that use the platform to deploy softwares without setting up dedicated technology teams.

QwikBuild’s Enterprise AI Play

QwikBuild combines custom software development with AI-driven workflow automation. Its platform allows businesses to build applications from scratch, replacing legacy systems or custom software layers on top of tools offered by giants like SAP and Salesforce. 

According to Ayyagari, the SaaS startup focuses on codifying business decisions rather than automating individual tasks alone.

For instance, a financial services company may need to decide which customers to contact, what filters to apply and which scripts to use for different customer segments. While a specialised AI startup may automate the calling process here, QwikBuild will look at codifying the decisions that determine which calls should be made in the first place.

Businesses can then autonomously deploy voice agents or other tools to execute these workflows, either through QwikBuild or other providers.

“Tech has always been the enabler. But adoption of tech was always the hardest problem that I have seen,” Ayyagari said, drawing on his experience at Flipkart, Swiggy and Slice.

QwikBuild aims to address this gap by allowing business teams to build and test applications as their requirements evolve, without repeatedly relying on engineering teams.

Ayyagari cited a recent customer meeting in which a business team discussed changes to an application. “The agent understood what the context was. The feature was immediately built within the next five minutes,” he said. “Tech and business can work parallelly together,” he added.

He also pointed to the potential for enterprise AI adoption. “Hardly 1% of enterprises have adopted AI. It’s a huge market that needs to be unlocked,” he said, adding that the software needed to automate businesses over the next five years would be “at least 10X” in price when compared with what’s available today.

The startup is betting that businesses will increasingly turn to platforms combining software development, integrations and AI agents to automate operations.

This is also reflected in recent enterprise AI investment trends in the Indian startup ecosystem,  For instance, enterprise AI and automation startup RapidCanvas netted $29 Mn last week. On a broader level, Indian AI startup funding surged 265% YoY to $438 Mn in Q3 2026, according to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report. 

However, Inc42’s survey of 85+ institutional investors found that 63% saw some degree of froth in AI valuations, with about half of them expecting a correction within 18 months. Despite these concerns, investors see vertical AI as the biggest value driver over the next five years, followed by AI hardware and semiconductors and AI-led IT and business services.

item.title: Nova Spectral AI Raises ₹21.2 Cr To Build Indigenous Infrared Sensor Chips
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Bengaluru-based Nova Spectral AI has raised ₹21.2 Cr ($2.3 Mn) in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based Nova Spectral AI has raised ₹21.2 Cr ($2.3 Mn) in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors.

Founded earlier this year by IIT Kanpur alum Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, Nova Spectral is building short-wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chips using colloidal quantum dots (cQDs) and standard silicon CMOS manufacturing processes. 

This will help drones, surveillance systems, robots and autonomous vehicles capture images in low-light conditions and through smoke, haze and dust. It aims to develop an indigenous alternative to conventional infrared sensors, which are largely imported and rely on expensive indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) technology.

The fresh capital will help the startup expand its team as well as develop a field-ready prototype within 18 months.

“India’s armed forces should not have to rely on an imported sensor to see at night or through smoke. We design and build our chip in India, with a roadmap to make the quantum dot materials and readout chip here too,” Nova Spectral AI cofounder and CEO Priyadarshi said.

Nova Spectral AI was founded earlier this year by Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar. Priyadarshi has built a quantum dot fabrication facility from the ground up and developed working indium arsenide sensors for SWIR imaging.

It also secured in-principle approval to incubate at IISc Bengaluru, where it planned to expand its team after the seed round.

The investment comes at a time when India’s deeptech sector continues to draw investor interest in strategic hardware and domestic chip design. Policy tailwinds from India’s indigenisation push, alongside support for semiconductor design and defence electronics manufacturing, have helped sharpen investor focus on locally built sensing technologies.

As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. 

In this light, investors continue to launch funds to back startups in the deeptech space, where Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising a ₹700 Cr venture capital fund to back AI and deeptech startups, under the name Longshot Capital, a Category II AIF. 

Prior to that, South Korean gaming giant KRAFTON disclosed its plans to invest an additional $250 Mn (₹3,300 Cr) in Indian startups across areas such as AI, robotics and deeptech over the next three to four years.

item.title: Exclusive: Ex-Pixxel Engineer Effy John’s Parsec Aerospace In Talks To Raise $10 Mn
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Aerospace technology startup Parsec Aerospace, founded by former Pixxel engineer Effy John, is in talks to raise around $10 Mn…
item.content:encoded:
Aerospace technology startup Parsec Aerospace, founded by former Pixxel engineer Effy John, is in talks to raise around $10 Mn (about ₹95 Cr) in a funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, sources told Inc42. 

The funding round is also expected to see participation from existing investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners, the sources added.

The Bengaluru-based startup is developing next-generation engines for aerospace applications and remains in stealth mode. Details about its engine technology, target customers, commercialisation plans, and proposed use of the fresh capital are not publicly available.

Queries sent to Parsec Aerospace and Nexus Venture Partners did not elicit a response by the time of publication.

John founded Parsec Aerospace after working at spacetech startup Pixxel, which develops hyperspectral imaging satellites and Earth-observation technology.

Parsec Aerospace was incorporated in September 2025, according to publicly available corporate records.

Rising Investor Interest In Deeptech

The funding talks come amid increased capital deployment into India’s deeptech ecosystem, spanning aerospace, defence technology, robotics, and semiconductors.

Indian deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals in Q3 2026 compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in the corresponding quarter last year. Funding rose nearly 2.8X, although the number of deals edged lower.

Among recent investments, metal additive manufacturing startup ThinkMetal raised ₹27 Cr in a round led by IAN Alpha Fund earlier this month. The startup builds industrial printing systems used to manufacture tools such as moulds, dies, jigs, and fixtures.

In September, Aeron Systems raised ₹45 Cr in a pre-Series B round jointly led by Riverwalk Holdings and MGF-Kavachh. It develops inertial navigation and weather-monitoring systems for aerospace, defence, renewable energy, and other industrial applications.

More directly in aerospace propulsion, D-Propulse Aerospace raised ₹25 Cr from IAN Alpha Fund earlier this year to develop propulsion systems for defence and aerospace applications.

item.title: Live2.ai Raises ₹130 Cr To Scale AI Marketing SaaS Platform
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Live2.ai has raised ₹130 Cr ($13.7 Mn) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures.…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based AI startup Live2.ai has raised ₹130 Cr ($13.7 Mn) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The fundraise comprises both a fresh issue as well as a secondary component providing partial liquidity to undisclosed early investors. The AI-powered SaaS startup’s board features backers like Sony Innovation Fund, SOSV and Duane Park.

The startup, which offers enterprises a SaaS platform that helps them monitor engagement for campaigns across channels, will use the fresh capital to build its AI platform further, strengthen its go-to-market strategy for enterprise customers and global consumer brands and expand regional cloud infrastructure. 

It also plans to hire across engineering, data science and customer success teams in North America, Europe, Singapore and India.

“Brands today are drowning in signals and starved of action. Every conversation, creator post and trend spike is a revenue decision waiting to be made, and most are made too late or not at all. This funding lets us close that gap, with detection, decision and activation running in one governed loop for enterprise customers across North America, Europe and APAC,” said CEO and cofounder J Venkat. 

Founded by Venkat, Neha Suyal and Yash Arora, Live2.ai’s social intelligence platform monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X, and review sites. 

It combines social listening and trend identification with influencer content auditing, campaign compliance, social publishing, and performance tracking. It also enables brands to convert content into shoppable experiences across channels. 

The platform’s major differentiator lies in how it runs eight AI agents, including tools for crisis detection, trend identification, campaign auditing and automated responses, with governance controls and human review mechanisms.

Live2.ai said its revenue grew fourfold in the past 12 months, with only 10% of its revenue coming from the Indian market. Its clientele includes names like Bonkers Corner, Drools, Enamor, Henkel, Bliscent, among others.

Organisations are increasingly turning to AI to automate workflows across functions, and marketing is no exception. Nutanix’s cofounder Ajeet Singh recently launched a new venture Different, describing it as an AI marketing system to automate demand generation. 

Enterprise players are also acquiring AI startups to bring such capabilities in-house. Global software giant Adobe acquired agentic AI martech startup Rilo last month, while SaaS major MoEngage acquired Aampe to augment its agentic marketing initiatives.

item.title: Healthy Snacking Brand Troovy Bags ₹100 Cr To Expand Offline Presence, Enter New Categories
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Healthy snacking brand Troovy has raised ₹100 Cr ($10.5 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by existing investor…
item.content:encoded:
Healthy snacking brand Troovy has raised ₹100 Cr ($10.5 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by existing investor Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures.

The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its manufacturing capacity and fuel its research and development (R&D) for product development. The D2C brand will also strengthen its distribution across quick commerce and offline channels.

Besides, the startup plans to expand its portfolio into categories like namkeen, biscuits and cookies by January 2027, Baranwal said.

“We will also launch more products in existing categories and build our R&D capabilities. We’re planning to develop new products with parents, as well as innovators from across the country,” cofounder Mansi Baranwal told Inc42.

Founded in 2021 by husband-and-wife duo Mansi Baranwal and Aditya Mukherjee, Troovy initially entered the market with clean-label ketchup and later expanded into the healthy snacking category.

Its portfolio of products includes chips, puffs, sauces, spreads, millet-based pasta, cookies and milk mixes. Chips and puffs are Troovy’s hero categories, together accounting for around 60-70% of sales, as per Baranwal. 

Troovy Doubles Down On Offline Expansion

Marketplaces and quick commerce account for roughly half of Troovy’s sales, while sales from its own website brings in about 30%. Offline retail, which the startup recently entered in Delhi NCR, accounts for close to 6% of revenue. 

Troovy has begun building its offline distribution network, starting with Delhi NCR and neighbouring areas. It plans to expand into select metro and Tier I markets, initially focusing on Delhi NCR, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with some presence planned in Punjab and Haryana.

Baranwal said the startup is taking a measured approach as it works out its distribution strategy for offline retail.

“We’re very much in learning mode. We’re trying to figure out the playbook and experiment with different things,” she said, adding that North India is an important market for chips.

The latest fundraise follows Troovy’s $5 Mn Series A round in January this year, led by Fireside Ventures. 

“Troovy grew 5X in the eight months following our last investment, and that is what made us double down,” said Ankita Balotia, principal at Fireside Ventures.

The latest fundraise announcement comes months after the startup came under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India’s (FSSAI) scrutiny over the use of the word “Healthy” in the names of its Veggie Chips, Ragi Chips and Moong Dal Chips. 

The regulator said the product names could mislead consumers, despite the products containing other ingredients. 

Responding to a question on the food regulator’s crackdown, Baranwal said stricter enforcement of food labelling rules could benefit brands that have invested in product formulation and ingredient transparency.

“I strongly think that this is great for the sector as well as for consumers and the country at large. These regulations exist for the benefit of the consumer, and tighter implementation is always better from a consumer perspective,” she said.

However, she said compliance could add to the costs and operational challenges faced by startups that lack adequate testing infrastructure.

“We do a lot of lab testing, and it puts a lot of pressure on startups like us that don’t have the correct infrastructure,” Baranwal said.

She added that Troovy was also working to reduce sodium levels in its products and limit the use of ingredients it considers undesirable.

item.title: [Update] SC Seeks Centre’s Response On News Publishers’ Plea Against DPDP Act
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update | October 27, 17:42 IST The Supreme Court today sought responses from the Centre and the Ministry of Electronics…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 27, 17:42 IST

The Supreme Court today sought responses from the Centre and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on a plea challenging provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023. However, the court declined to grant an interim stay on the law before hearing the government on the matter.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on the application seeking a stay. “No stay without hearing other side. But notice on stay application issued,” CJI Kant said.

The matter will be heard next on November 17.

The plea was filed by the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which represents 21 digital news publishers, including NDTV, Network 18, The Indian Express, India Today etc.

Original | October 27, 01:44 IST

A group of 21 news publishers has reportedly challenged India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court (SC), arguing that the law could undermine investigative journalism and expose journalists’ sources.

The lawsuit, filed on October 6, argues that the law’s provisions on consent, data erasure and government access to information could restrict news reporting and force publishers to remove factual stories. The case is scheduled to be heard on October 27, according to a Reuters report.

The challenge comes nearly a year after the Centre notified the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 in November last year. The broader DPDP Act, 2023 and the Rules establish a framework governing how organisations collect, process and protect individuals’ digital personal data.

The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which represents the publishers, has argued that the law does not provide a specific exemption for journalistic activities. According to the confidential filing, the association reportedly said that the absence of such safeguards could compromise press freedom and investigative reporting.

The DNPA’s members include Mukesh Ambani-owned Network18, Gautam Adani-owned NDTV, the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group.

Publishers Vs The DPDP Act

A key concern raised by the publishers is the requirement to obtain consent before processing personal data. The DNPA has argued that requiring journalists to notify the subjects of investigations and seek their consent could allow them to destroy evidence or intimidate witnesses.

The association has also flagged provisions allowing individuals to withdraw consent and request the erasure of their personal data. According to the filing, the absence of a public-interest safeguard could force publishers to remove or substantially redact factual news reports.

The publishers have further raised concerns about provisions empowering the government to seek information from organisations handling personal data. They argue that these powers could expose confidential journalistic sources and discourage whistleblowers from sharing information about corruption, corporate wrongdoing and electoral malpractice.

The filing also challenges the government’s power to restrict access to information in the public interest, arguing that the provisions could curtail press freedom.

The DNPA has sought the quashing of several contentious provisions of the law, most of which are scheduled to come into effect from May 2027, Reuters reported.

The association has also argued that the government has granted broad exemptions to the state without extending corresponding protections to the press.

What The DPDP Framework Provides

The DPDP Act, enacted in August 2023, establishes obligations for processing digital personal data. The later DPDP Rules, notified in November 2025, provide a phased implementation framework, giving organisations up to 18 months to comply with specified requirements.

The framework requires platforms to obtain consent for processing personal data, provide clear information about its use and implement security safeguards. It also gives individuals rights to access, correct, update and seek the erasure of their personal data, subject to the applicable provisions.

The latest case marks one of the most prominent challenges to the DPDP framework so far, raising questions about how India’s data protection requirements will interact with press freedom and investigative reporting.

The Act provides for financial penalties of up to ₹250 Cr for failing to implement reasonable security safeguards. Other violations, including certain breaches of obligations relating to children’s personal data, can attract penalties of up to ₹200 Cr.

However, the publishers argue that the framework does not adequately account for the requirements of investigative journalism, particularly when reporting involves personal information collected in the public interest.

The government has maintained that the framework protects citizens’ privacy while supporting responsible data processing.

item.title: Simplismart Bags $14 Mn To Expand AI Inference Platform
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: AI infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 Mn (around ₹133 Cr) in a Series B funding round led by Dallas…
item.content:encoded:
AI infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 Mn (around ₹133 Cr) in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC, Micromax, and angel investors.

Dallas Venture Capital invested close to $5 Mn in the round, cofounder and CEO Amritanshu Jain told Inc42.

Simplismart plans to use the fresh capital to further develop its AI inference platform, deepen partnerships with cloud providers and sovereign AI players, and expand across North America and other global markets.

AI inference is the process of running trained models to generate responses or predictions.

Founded in 2022 by Jain and Devansh Ghatak, Simplismart builds the software layer between AI models and GPU infrastructure. Its inference engine lets businesses configure how models run based on their speed, cost, and performance requirements, while its orchestration platform manages deployment and scaling across cloud and on-premises infrastructure.

“We have spent four years building the software layer between the model and the GPU, helping customers optimise how their workloads are deployed and operated. This funding will allow us to take that platform to more enterprises and cloud providers globally,” Jain said.

The funding will also support the development of a dynamic GPU scheduling layer to match AI workloads with available computing capacity across regions and time zones, cofounder and CTO Ghatak said.

How Simplismart Makes Money

Jain said Simplismart offers three deployment and pricing models: shared endpoints, dedicated endpoints, and bring-your-own-compute deployments.

Under the shared endpoint model, customers pay based on token consumption, without a minimum fee. Dedicated endpoints allow customers to rent GPU infrastructure along with Simplismart’s optimisation software, with charges linked to GPU usage and runtime.

The bring-your-own-compute model caters to businesses that want to run workloads on their own infrastructure to meet data and regulatory requirements, particularly in sectors such as banking, financial services, and insurance.

For its cloud-provider offering, Simplismart works with NVIDIA to help providers deploy and manage AI infrastructure at scale. The startup does not own the computing infrastructure. Instead, its software enables cloud providers to offer managed AI services under their own brands using their existing GPUs.

The startup said this offering is already being used by Yotta, with Simplismart powering the serverless inference layer of its Shakti Studio platform. This allows customers to run AI models without managing the underlying inference infrastructure themselves.

Around 55% of Simplismart’s revenue comes from the US, with the remainder generated in India, Jain said.

Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna, and Ema, which use its platform to run video, voice, multimodal, and enterprise AI workloads. Simplismart said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14X over the past six months.

Prior to this round, Simplismart raised $7 Mn in a Series A round led by Accel in October 2024.

The fundraise comes amid growing investment in India’s AI infrastructure ecosystem.

Tata Communications yesterday announced plans to invest $400 Mn to $450 Mn to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India. The proposed network will connect major data centres and AI hubs to support demand for high-speed, low-latency connectivity.

item.title: Why This Festive Season Is Getting More Expensive For Ecommerce Sellers
item.dc:creator: Bismah Malik
item.description: Consider a kurta priced at ₹799 sold directly on Flipkart by a fashion brand such as Globus Fashion. Since July,…
item.content:encoded:
Consider a kurta priced at ₹799 sold directly on Flipkart by a fashion brand such as Globus Fashion.

Since July, Flipkart stopped charging a commission on fashion products, so on paper the seller keeps more of each sale than it did a year ago.

But under Flipkart’s new penalty structure, effective August 23, the seller is penalised ₹30 the moment the kurta misses its dispatch-by date. 

If the order is then cancelled, the seller is penalised another ₹60. 

Flipkart now also counts three missed deadlines as a cancellation. But the flat penalty (a total of ₹90) means that sellers face a greater burden to clear low-value orders.  

This is one example of how selling online has become costlier this festive season, and penalties are just one part of it. Besides this, there are fee surcharges that apply to every order, whether or not it is delayed or cancelled. And the cost of production and fulfilment have also gone up due to issues ranging from a crunch in raw material supply as well as high fuel prices due to the instability in West Asia.  

No matter the seller, whether it is a brand or an Amazon-specific seller, these charges and surcharges are making it harder and costlier to sellers on ecommerce at a time when business is at its peak. 

Third-party sellers usually operate on thinner margins than brands and have no control over the price listed on Amazon India, according to industry sources we spoke to.

Some brands take up the operations themselves, depending on the marketplace. Globus Fashion, for instance, sells directly on Flipkart but through Cocoblu Retail on Amazon. 

Another brand, Ruhe India, which sells smart kitchen and smart home products, holds its own seller account and sells directly on the marketplaces. The approach is different but the charges will remain. 

The changes coincide with the peak festive season sales on Amazon India and Flipkart. According to Redseer projections, festive ecommerce GMV will reach $15–16 Bn in 2026, up about 25% from roughly $12.5 Bn in 2025, with online festive shoppers rising to 180–185 Mn from 160 Mn. 

But these estimates do not account for the higher cost that customers and sellers will have to pay for using the ecommerce platform. And that’s before we even account for the potential slowdown due to the merchant discount rate or MDR coming up in merchant UPI payments.  

The New Penalty Structure

On August 17, months before its main festive season shopping window, Amazon changed how it charges cancellation fees for sellers on Easy Ship and Self Ship.

Under Easy Ship, Amazon picks up the order from the seller and delivers it; under Self Ship, the seller delivers it through its own courier. 

The fee, earlier tied to flat category-based referral charges, is now a percentage of the order value, according to Amazon’s communication to sellers. Amazon now charges 10% of the order value on orders up to ₹10,000, 8% between ₹10,001 and ₹50,000, 5% between ₹50,001 and ₹1 lakh, and 2% above that, plus 18% GST.

A cancelled ₹30,000 order can end up costing the seller about ₹2,832 including the GST which is applicable on cancellation fee. Sellers of electronics, appliances and other big-ticket goods carry the most exposure per order. 

“This fee is conditional and only applies in the rare event of a seller-initiated cancellation, which accounts for less than 1% of orders on Amazon.in. We have appropriate measures in place to ensure sellers are protected when cancellations are due to circumstances beyond their control,” Amazon told Inc42 in an emailed statement.

Electronics sellers are already under pressure due to expectations that the 2026 winter season will result in slower sales than 2025. This is largely due to the rising prices of mobile devices and electronics this year, but the extra charges will also play a role in whether sellers even offer some products for sale.  

Flipkart did not respond to Inc42’s queries. 

People familiar with the company’s operations said the penalties follow its zero-commission push, which has nearly doubled seller onboarding year-on-year. In July, Flipkart dropped commissions across its fashion catalogue, removing an earlier ₹1,000 price ceiling for the waiver.

Whose Fault Is A Delay?

The platforms’ position is that penalties apply only when sellers fail. Sellers, however, claim the line is not always clear.

Responding to Amazon’s notices on its seller forum, some sellers said cancellations were sometimes caused by delivery personnel failing to turn up for scheduled pickups, and asked why the fee should apply in such cases.

A founder of a snacking brand, who wished to be anonymous, told us when a logistics-side delay gets billed to the seller instead of the carrier, this becomes a source of friction and can disrupt many smaller sellers. “We have contested such cases with evidence of timely dispatch, but found the process cumbersome,” the founder added. 

Kapil Gupta, founder of Ruhe India, whose catalogue runs from sub-₹500 to ₹3,000-plus, told Inc42 that  Flipkart’s flat ₹90 penalty would land hardest on the brand’s value-tier catalogue.

Vinod Kumar, trustee of the Forum for Internet Resellers, Sellers and Traders (FIRST INDIA), said online sellers accept the need for timely fulfilment, but the increase in fees and penalties just before the festive season is a concern for MSMEs already dealing with thin margins and rising costs this year. 

Unlike the penalties, these charges apply regardless of seller performance, which seems like a blanket rule meant to punish even those who have a very low proportion of cancellations or delays. 

Deliveries Turn Costlier Too

What makes matters worse is that delivery fees and logistics costs have gone up across the industry, meaning no brand or seller is immune to this. 

From September 7, Amazon raised its closing fee, a flat per-item charge separate from the commission, by ₹1 on products priced up to ₹500 and by ₹3 or higher-priced items. Amazon’s seller fee page attributes the increase to higher fuel and logistics costs.

Similarly, Flipkart’s logistics arm is mulling a revision in fulfillment fees for sellers, according to sources. 

Logistics platform Delhivery added a surcharge on D2C shipments of ₹4 per express shipment and ₹2 per surface shipment, on top of contracted rates from September 1,. The company has reportedly attributed it to higher aviation turbine fuel prices, ground-staff costs and inflation across its network. 

The new pricing structure affects a specific group: brands shipping orders from their own websites. Delhivery declined to comment to Inc42 related to queries on increase in the pricings.

Ruhe India’s Gupta said the surcharge would be a challenge for brands building native website sales, which rely on third-party logistics players such as Delhivery.

Globus Fashion, which sells directly and through marketplace sellers, said that logistics or fulfillment costs “can be renegotiated between the brand and marketplace”, but others say that this is not a standardised process. 

The fashion brand expects festive logistics spending to rise with demand, but does not expect a big impact on revenue, because inventory placement and warehouse use have already been allocated ahead of time. 

Large enterprises stock regional warehouses months in advance to lock in contracted freight rates and accept the holding costs. Other brands may not have these pieces in place. 

But, freight operators see more and more brands responding to the festive rush ahead of time. Geetali Sunil Khare, founder of Rachana Speed Logistics, said brands and wholesalers are building inventory ahead of the rush rather than cutting order sizes to protect margins, to avoid stockouts and supply disruptions at peak demand.

In categories such as electronics and apparel, sellers need to retain minimal stock to avoid post-festive inventory risk, and absorb higher, fragmented spot freight costs instead. Truck rental rates in September held above year-ago levels, but month-on-month increases across most corridors have been relatively modest, Khare added. 

The bigger festive challenge, she said, is meeting tighter service expectations with higher shipment volumes and heavier consignments.

“On the logistics side it is mostly the truck movement to warehouses that makes up for substantial expenses operation wise. With the deliveries now expanding to regional markets , it makes it harder to to fill vehicles on the way out and leaving return legs empty or under-used,” Aman Mahlawat, founder of Mahlawat Logistics, added.

On local runs, Mahlawat said, highway transit is smooth, but city entry restrictions and long queues at distribution hub docks cause major delays.

Quick commerce, according to the industry players we spoke to, has also added to the cost-strain. High-frequency replenishment of dark store inventory is changing how stock moves upstream from warehouses to the distribution endpoints. 

Mahlawat said dark stores and retailers now prefer frequent, smaller drops to monthly bulk dispatches, which splits loads into smaller vehicles and leaves trucks spending more hours waiting at congested unloading docks than moving on the road.  These frequent, fragmented dispatches need constant vehicle availability, squeezing truck turnaround times and load consolidation.

“More predictability, enough lead time on fee and policy changes to plan for them, rather than absorbing them mid-season is the only way sellers or brands can work around these changes,” Ruhe India’s Gupta added.’

Can Commission Cuts Offset Rising Costs?

While Flipkart, Amazon India and others have cut commissions for sellers this year, the rising logistics costs, the extra charges this year, and the growing dependency on advertising spending on marketplaces have eaten into the margins of sellers. 

Amazon waived referral fees on products under ₹1,000 in March, and Flipkart extended zero commission to all fashion categories in July. Those cuts cover specific categories and price bands while closing fees, shipping charges and penalties apply across categories

Sellers are bemoaning the lack of clarity on when new charges are introduced or why they are applicable to all sellers regardless of their past performance. What sellers are asking for is more predictability from marketplaces and platforms, especially around the peak festive season.

item.title: IndiaMART Q2 Profit Rises 10% YoY To ₹91 Cr
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: B2B ecommerce platform IndiaMART InterMESH’s net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) rose 9.8% YoY to ₹90.7 Cr from…
item.content:encoded:
B2B ecommerce platform IndiaMART InterMESH’s net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) rose 9.8% YoY to ₹90.7 Cr from ₹82.6 Cr in the year ago quarter. Sequentially, profit tanked by 47.3% from ₹172.2 Cr.

IndiaMART’s operating revenue grew 10% YoY and 3.4% QoQ to ₹428.6 Cr in the quarter. However, negative other income of ₹7.6 Cr pulled total income down to ₹421 Cr. The company said interest income on financial assets measured at amortised cost is recognised under other income using the effective interest rate method.

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter rose 2.7% YoY to ₹276.3 Cr. The company’s share of losses from associates widened to ₹15.3 Cr from ₹13.4 Cr a year earlier. The company’s tax expense for the quarter stood at ₹38.6 Cr.

EBITDA for the quarter fell by about 2% YoY to ₹156 Cr,  while EBITDA margin improved by 300 bps to 40%. 

Customer collections grew 9% YoY to ₹443 Cr in Q2 FY27. This included ₹394 Cr from IndiaMART’s standalone business and ₹46 Cr from Busy Infotech.

IndiaMART claims to have registered unique business enquiries of 2.7 Cr in Q2FY27. 

Supplier Storefronts grew 4% YoY to 89 Lakh and paying suppliers at the end of the quarter stood 2.2 Lakh. Annualised revenue per paying supplier increased 10% to about ₹72,000, helping support marketplace revenue growth.

“Our efforts to strengthen platform trustworthiness are fostering greater confidence and deeper, more meaningful engagement across the marketplace. AI remains central to enhancing user experience, from discovery and matchmaking to conversational tools, while we also explore new monetisation avenues. With a robust business model and strong cash generation, we remain well positioned to create long-term value for all our stakeholders,” CEO Dinesh Agarwal said.

Shares of IndiaMART ended today’s trading session 4.09% higher at ₹1,625.95 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Mochatrade Raises $5.5 Mn To Build A US Stock Trading Platform For Indian Traders
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Fintech startup Mochatrade, which offers US Stock tokens trading platform for Indian traders, announced the raise of $5.5 Mn (₹52.3…
item.content:encoded:
Fintech startup Mochatrade, which offers US Stock tokens trading platform for Indian traders, announced the raise of $5.5 Mn (₹52.3 Cr) in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures, among others.

The startup will use the fresh capital to bolster its trading engine and risk infrastructure and expand its reach among active Indian traders.

Founded in 2026 by Utkarsh Sinha, Chetan Manda and Parth Maheshwari, Mochatrade is building a trading platform that allows Indian retail traders and global investors to trade perpetual futures and price-tracking contracts linked to US stocks, cryptocurrencies, commodities and major indices.

Its waitlist has crossed 25,000 sign-ups, although it is yet to announce a public launch date.

The platform is expected to allow users to fund their accounts through UPI and track balances, margins and profit and loss (P&L) in Indian rupees (INR). 

The platform’s perpetual futures contracts will allow traders to take long or short positions based on their expectations of price movements, without owning the underlying assets. Unlike conventional futures contracts, these instruments have no fixed expiry date.

Mochatrade will also offer leveraged trading, allowing users to take larger positions with less upfront capital. However, leverage can amplify losses as well as gains. The startup plans to earn revenue through trading fees and eventually introduce contracts linked to select pre-IPO companies, US stock options and social trading features, subject to regulatory approvals.

“India traded $1.9 Tn in options premium turnover last year. The appetite to trade is already here. But when Indians want to trade the US market, the product still feels foreign,” said Sinha, CEO of Mochatrade.

Sinha previously cofounded crypto wallet Martian in 2022, which recorded more than 2 Mn installs and $2 Bn in transaction volume. Martian raised $3.6 Mn from Race Capital, Superscrypt and Jump Crypto before being acquired by Lightspeed-backed Pontem.

Manda became Sprinklr’s youngest director of product in 2025, while Maheshwari worked on Photoshop for the web at Adobe before leading payments and credit infrastructure at Navi.

Mochatrade is entering the market as Indian investors increasingly look overseas for exposure to global assets, particularly US stocks. 

According to RBI data, Indian residents remitted $2.65 Bn overseas for equity and debt investments in FY26, up from $1.51 Bn in FY24. Remittances reached $1.4 Bn between April and July FY27, with July alone accounting for $344.6 Mn, a 121% year-on-year increase. These figures cover overseas equity and debt investments across markets, rather than US stocks alone.

At the same time, regulatory changes are reshaping India’s domestic trading market. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has tightened futures and options (F&O) rules to curb excessive speculation and protect retail investors. 

Measures include limiting weekly expiries to one benchmark index per exchange, increasing contract sizes and tightening margin requirements. The changes have weighed on trading activity and revenue at several brokerage platforms, including Zerodha and Groww, during FY26.

Against this backdrop, Mochatrade is betting that demand for global market exposure will create an opportunity for a trading platform built around Indian users. Its ability to convert waitlist interest into active traders will depend on its product experience, risk controls and the regulatory framework governing the contracts it plans to offer.

item.title: SoftBank Sells 1.2% Stake In Ola Electric, Offloads 1.12 Cr Rights Entitlements
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Japanese tech investor SoftBank has sold another 1.2% stake in Ola Electric through a series of open market transactions between…
item.content:encoded:
Japanese tech investor SoftBank has sold another 1.2% stake in Ola Electric through a series of open market transactions between January 6 and October 22, reducing its holding in the electric two-wheeler maker to 11.7%.

Its investment vehicle, SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC, sold 5.55 Cr shares during the period, leaving it with 54.15 Cr shares. The filing pegged its holding before the transactions at 12.9%, calculated using the company’s latest share capital. 

The SoftBank entity also sold 1.12 Cr rights entitlements during the period, even as Ola Electric looks to raise nearly ₹1,000 Cr through a rights issue to repay debt and fund expansion.

SoftBank received 4.33 Cr rights entitlements against the 54.15 Cr shares it held on the October 13 record date, under the issue’s two-for-25 ratio. It sold approximately 25.9% of these entitlements, leaving it with 3.21 Cr as of October 22.

Rights entitlements allow eligible shareholders to subscribe to additional shares at the issue price. Shareholders can exercise these entitlements or transfer them to other investors. Selling an entitlement does not reduce their existing equity holding.

SoftBank first backed Ola Electric in July 2019 with a $250 Mn investment that valued the EV maker at around $1 Bn. It participated in a subsequent funding round in September 2021, when Ola Electric’s valuation rose to $3 Bn.

The Japanese investor has progressively reduced its holding since the company went public in August 2024.

In January this year, SoftBank disclosed the sale of 9.46 Cr shares, or a 2.15% stake, through open market transactions between September 3, 2025, and January 5. That disclosure put its holding after the sales at 13.53%. The latest filing calculates the pre-sale holding using Ola Electric’s expanded share capital.

Before that, the investor sold another 9.4 Cr shares, representing a 2.15% stake, between July and September 2025.

Another Round Of Fundraising

Ola Electric is seeking additional capital to stabilise its core electric scooter business while investing in battery manufacturing and energy storage.

Its ₹999.74 Cr rights issue opened on October 22 and will close on October 30. It comprises up to 37.03 Cr partly paid-up equity shares priced at ₹27 apiece.

Investors must pay ₹16.20 per share on application, with the remaining ₹10.80 payable through a subsequent call.

In June, Ola Electric raised ₹780.24 Cr through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), exceeding its initial target of ₹500 Cr. It had earmarked ₹225 Cr from the net proceeds for debt repayment, ₹335 Cr for organic growth, and the remainder for general corporate purposes.

Meanwhile, Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares on the opening day of the rights issue.

Motilal Oswal applied for approximately 1.28 Cr shares against entitlements transferred by ANI Technologies, an Ola Electric promoter-group entity. Calliope applied for another 1.1 Cr shares against entitlements transferred by Indus Trust, another promoter-group entity.

Revenue Decline Adds Pressure

The fundraise comes as Ola Electric steps up investments in battery cell manufacturing and battery energy storage systems while pursuing a broader business reset. This includes shifting towards dealer-operated stores and rolling out more affordable electric scooters.

The company’s consolidated operating revenue fell 45% to ₹455 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹828 Cr in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. Its net loss, however, narrowed 21.5% to ₹336 Cr from ₹428 Cr. It is yet to announce its Q2 FY27 results.

Ola Electric is also battling to regain ground in the electric two-wheeler market. Its market share fell to 6.5% in September from 7.6% in August.

Earlier this month, Goldman Sachs downgraded its recommendation on the stock to ‘Sell’ from ‘Neutral’ and cut its target price to ₹23 per share.

Shares of Ola Electric ended today’s trading session 16.775 higher at ₹34.95 on the BSE.

item.title: Luxury Watch Brand Rotoris Raises $8.5 Mn To Grow Retail Footprint
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Luxury watch brand Rotoris has raised $8.5 Mn (₹80.9 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures.…
item.content:encoded:
Luxury watch brand Rotoris has raised $8.5 Mn (₹80.9 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from 100Unicorns, Centricity, Diwakar Goel’s family office, Atul Singh’s family office, Adhiraj Burman’s family office, and Rannvijay Singha.

The D2C startup said it would deploy the fresh capital towards research and development, expanding production capacity, and growing its Rotoris House retail footprint in India and overseas, including Mumbai and New York.

Founded in 2025 by Bella Vita’s founder Aakash Anand, Wolfpack Labs’ founding partner Prerna Gupta, and Drink Free Advertising Media’s cofounders Anant Narula and Kunal Kapania, Rotoris aims to build “India’s first global watch brand”. It operates as a luxury watch brand, selling limited-edition watches through an invitation-only membership programme called the Rotoris Registry.

Rotoris assembles and tests its watches at its Rotoris Atelier in Gurugram, using machinery sourced from Switzerland. The startup said its assembly processes were established with guidance from Swiss horologists with experience at watchmakers and luxury brands such as Patek Philippe, IWC and Tiffany & Co.

“The design creates the desire, but the engineering, assembly and attention to detail earn the trust. We are building both sides of Rotoris with the same level of intention,” Gupta said.

The startup launched its first collection of 2,100 numbered watches in February 2026, which it claims sold out within days. Since then, nearly 1 Lakh people have registered for access to its collections, with around 40% of demand coming from international markets, including the US, Dubai and Australia.

Prior to this round, Rotoris bagged $3 Mn in a seed funding round co-led by Zerodha’s Nikhil Kamath, VC firms Venture Catalysts and 100Unicorns as well as actor Vivek Oberoi and content creator Tanmay Bhat, in December last year.

The country’s luxury watch market size is expected to grow at a 5.7% CAGR from $1.8 Bn in 2025 to $2.9 Bn by 2034. In this growing market, the analog watch segment holds the leading type share at 62.4% in 2025, while the men’s segment leads end user demand at 48.9%.

Rotoris bids to challenge the legacy luxury watch brands like Seiko, Tissot, Citizen, and Rado, who have established a strong foothold in the segment. Beside the Aakash Anand-led startup, Bangalore Watch Company and Jaipur Watch Company are also emerging contenders in the premium watch category.

item.title: Cent Raises $15 Mn To Scale AI-Led Preventive Healthcare Platform
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Healthtech startup Cent, launched by Practo cofounder Shashank ND earlier this year, announced the raise of $15 Mn (about ₹143…
item.content:encoded:
Healthtech startup Cent, launched by Practo cofounder Shashank ND earlier this year, announced the raise of $15 Mn (about ₹143 Cr) in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and existing investor South Park Commons (SPC), with participation from individual investors including former Vodafone CEO Arun Sarin and former OpenAI B2B CTO Srinivas Narayanan, among others. 

The fresh capital will be deployed to strengthen the preventive healthcare startup’s R&D function. Besides, the startup also intends to expand its AI, engineering and clinical teams. 

Apart from the fundraise, Cent also announced the acquisition of Medsee, an AI-powered radiology reporting workflow platform, to help it deliver faster and more consistent reporting as scan volumes increase.

Cent was launched by Shashank, along with ex-Ola Electric CMO Anshul Khandelwal and former Lenskart product head Arpit Garg earlier this year. It last raised a $5 Mn seed funding round back then from OneFlow Holdings and South Park Commons.

Bidding to build a positioning of helping users live a hundred years, Cent combines precision radiology, AI, and biomarkers to screen asymptomatic patients for over 300 conditions like cardiac disease, cancer, and neurological disorders.

Its flagship offering, Cent Check, combines full-body MRI, low-dose CT, DEXA scans, ECG, echocardiography in a single visit lasting around two hours. Its proprietary CCNM protocol is designed to assess cancer, cardiac, neurological and metabolic health risks. 

It uses AI to consolidate findings from different diagnostic modalities and generate organ-level risk assessments, while AI-assisted imaging helps reduce MRI scan times, with an aim to identify serious conditions before symptoms begin to surface.

Its comprehensive health screening package is priced at ₹27,500, positioning itself as an alternative to conventional preventive health checkups that largely rely on blood tests and limited imaging.

The startup said it has completed 10,000 preventive whole-body scans across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR since inception. It aims to scale this to 1 Cr scans by 2035.

Cent plans to use the data generated through its scans to establish health baselines for asymptomatic Indians, train models to identify disease risks earlier and support clinical research.

item.title: Ministry Of Defence Partners With Sarvam To Drive AI Adoption For Armed Forces
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Sarvam has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to advance AI adoption across Indian…
item.content:encoded:
Sarvam has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to advance AI adoption across Indian armed forces — Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force.

“HQ Integrated Defence Staff and Sarvam AI have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on AI applications, research, knowledge management, training and decision-support across the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force,” the ministry said in a post on social media. 

While the MoU marks Sarvam’s maiden push into defence, it comes at a time when the Central government’s focus on homegrown defencetech has picked up significantly. India is also looking to expand the use of indigenous AI capabilities across critical sectors.

The partnership is expected to support the development of AI-based solutions tailored to the requirements of the armed forces, although specific applications, deployment timelines and financial details of the partnership haven’t been disclosed.

At its inaugural developer conference in August, Sarvam Epoch, the startup outlined ambitions across the AI ecosystem. Its plans span across AI models, compute infrastructure, coding agents, voice technology, document intelligence and workplace applications, alongside hardware such as smart glasses.

The startup is betting that the Indian ecosystem will seek AI solutions which are more competitively priced, ensure data sovereignty and can deliver stronger performances. 

Its India-hosted infrastructure and language capabilities potentially give it an advantage in government, defence and regulated sectors. Its Anvaya platform targets defence and intelligence applications, including on-premise deployments.

Meanwhile, AI is expected to drive significant growth in India’s defence tech market. As per Inc42’s India’s Defence Tech Startup Ecosystem Report 2025, India’s defence tech market is projected to grow from $7.6 Bn in 2025 to $19 Bn by 2030, at a CAGR of 20%, with advanced technologies like AI expected to account for 48% of the market by 2030, up from 28% in 2025.

AI adoption is expanding, with 89% of Indian defence tech startups reporting its integration into their offerings. As demand grows for autonomous systems, AI-powered surveillance and advanced communications, indigenous innovation could become central to India’s defence modernisation. The challenge is to translate growing investment and adoption into sophisticated, reliable systems that strengthen technological self-reliance.

item.title: Baillie Gifford Funds Slash Value Of Holdings In Dailyhunt Parent VerSe By Up To 80%
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: VerSe Innovation, the parent of news aggregator Dailyhunt and short-video platform Josh, has seen two investment funds managed by Baillie…
item.content:encoded:
VerSe Innovation, the parent of news aggregator Dailyhunt and short-video platform Josh, has seen two investment funds managed by Baillie Gifford mark down the value of their holdings by around 80% over different periods.

Pacific Horizon Investment Trust valued its holding in VerSe at £4.08 Mn as of July 2026, down 51.4% from £8.39 Mn a year earlier. The holding’s value has fallen 80.3% from £20.69 Mn ($27.7 Mn) in July 2024.

Separately, The Schiehallion Fund valued its VerSe holding at $7.47 Mn as of August 2026, down 78.2% from $34.31 Mn in January 2025.

ET reported that Schiehallion’s investment represented a 1.3% stake in VerSe, implying a company valuation of about $576 Mn – nearly 90% below its $5 Bn valuation in 2022.

The implied valuation reflects the fund’s assessment of its investment, rather than a price established through a fresh funding round.

VerSe’s $5 Bn Valuation Under Pressure

VerSe last raised a major funding round in April 2022, when it secured $805 Mn at a reported valuation of $5 Bn.

In August 2024, TechCrunch reported that investor 360 ONE had valued VerSe at around $2.9 Bn, about 42% below its 2022 valuation.

VerSe disputed that interpretation, saying the assessment did not represent its overall valuation and that other investors continued to value it at around $5 Bn. At the time, the company also said it had not conducted a price-discovery funding round since April 2022.

The latest portfolio disclosures show that investors continue to reassess the value of their holdings. However, they do not establish a definitive company-wide valuation.

Founded in 2007 by Virendra Gupta and later joined by cofounder Umang Bedi, VerSe Innovation operates news aggregator Dailyhunt and short-video platform Josh. The company has raised nearly $1.7 Bn across funding rounds from investors including Google, Microsoft, Peak XV Partners, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, and Luxor Capital.

Revenue Growth, Lower Burn

Schiehallion had flagged concerns about VerSe’s performance in its interim report for the six months ended July 2025. The fund cited a deterioration in the company’s trajectory, including declining revenue, as the reason for a substantial downward revaluation during that period.

VerSe subsequently reported an improvement in its FY25 financial performance. According to the company, operating revenue rose 88% to ₹1,930 Cr from ₹1,029 Cr in FY24. Excluding acquisitions, operating revenue grew 33% to ₹1,373 Cr.

Its EBITDA burn, excluding non-cash expenses, narrowed 20% to ₹738 Cr from ₹920 Cr.

VerSe has been betting on acquisitions and adtech to diversify revenue. Its 2024 acquisition of Valueleaf was intended to strengthen advertiser targeting through NexVerse.ai, while Magzter expanded its subscription content business beyond advertising.

Meanwhile, Josh has faced declining users and monetisation challenges, prompting it to explore paid audio calls and other revenue streams. VerSe has also been automating manual processes as part of its shift towards AI-led operations.

item.title: Ather Energy Shares Jump 8% After HSBC, Nomura Raise Price Targets
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update| October 27, 17:32 IST Shares of Ather Energy ended today’s trading session 6.6% higher at ₹1,671 apiece on the…
item.content:encoded:
Update| October 27, 17:32 IST

Shares of Ather Energy ended today’s trading session 6.6% higher at ₹1,671 apiece on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to ₹66,291.5 Cr ($6.9 Bn).

Original| October 27, 11:55 IST

Shares of Ather Energy jumped as much as 8.1% to an intraday high of ₹1,702 on the BSE after HSBC and Nomura raised their price targets following the electric two-wheeler maker’s Q2 FY27 results.

At 11:28 IST, the stock was trading 6.8% higher at ₹1,680.60, giving the company a market capitalisation of ₹66,672.4 Cr (about $6.9 Bn).

The gains extended yesterday’s rally, when Ather shares closed 13.7% higher at ₹1,574 on the BSE after the company announced its Q2 FY27 results during market hours.

Adding to the positive sentiment, HSBC and Nomura retained their ‘Buy’ ratings and raised their price targets, citing better-than-expected margins and stronger growth prospects following the launch of Ather’s Konarc scooter range.

HSBC raised its price target to ₹1,800 from ₹1,600. The brokerage said Ather delivered a strong second quarter, with EBITDA breaking even ahead of expectations despite commodity cost pressures.

Nomura increased its price target to ₹2,070 from ₹1,926. It said Ather’s EBITDA margin, excluding other income, stood at 0.8%, beating its estimate of negative 2.6% and the consensus estimate of negative 2.7%. Stronger bookings and improved growth visibility following the Konarc launch were other positives.

Ather’s Maiden Profitable Quarter

Ather reported a consolidated net profit of ₹1.3 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against a loss of ₹154.1 Cr a year earlier, supported by stronger revenue growth, improving margins, and other income. It had posted a net loss of ₹51.1 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Operating revenue rose 62.9% YoY and 20.3% QoQ to ₹1,464.2 Cr. Including other income, EBITDA stood at ₹74.2 Cr, with a margin of 4.9% as against -9.6% a year earlier and 0.8% in Q1 FY27.

Total income rose to ₹1,527 Cr from ₹940.7 Cr a year earlier. However, operating revenue remained ₹61.5 Cr below total expenses of ₹1,525.7 Cr, underscoring other income’s contribution to net profitability.

CEO Tarun Mehta said during the earnings call that Ather would prioritise capacity expansion and sales growth over near-term net profitability. He cautioned that some margin gains came from temporary measures, including changes to its product mix and reduced incentives, which offered limited scope for further support if commodity prices remained elevated. 

Ather To Expand Manufacturing Capacity

Ather plans to invest ₹122 Cr to expand manufacturing capacity at its Hosur plant in Tamil Nadu and its upcoming Factory 3.0 in Maharashtra’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The expansion is expected to add 2.25 Lakh units of annual capacity.

At Hosur, the company plans to invest up to ₹58 Cr, including taxes, to add capacity for 75,000 units annually by December 2026. Ather has also earmarked ₹53 Cr for a new battery line, which is expected to be completed by Q3 FY28.

At Factory 3.0, the company plans to invest ₹64 Cr to add 1.5 Lakh units of annual capacity to the planned 5 Lakh units. The expansion is expected to be completed by Q2 FY28.

Ather will finance the investments through a combination of debt and internal accruals. During Q2 FY27, it also raised ₹1,300 Cr through a qualified institutions placement and ₹200 Cr through a preferential equity allotment.

The expansion follows a sharp increase in customer interest. Enquiries rose 109% YoY to around 10 Lakh in Q2 FY27, while pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 Lakh. Vehicle sales increased 42% to 93,211 units.

Ather launched its sub-₹1 Lakh Konarc electric scooter range during the quarter, taking its portfolio to 15 variants across three product lines.

item.title: WeWork India Q2 Profit Jumps 219% To ₹20 Cr, Revenue Rises 34% YoY
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Flexible workspace provider WeWork India reported a 219% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹20.4 Cr in the September…
item.content:encoded:
Flexible workspace provider WeWork India reported a 219% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹20.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 from ₹6.4 Cr in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, as revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses. 

The company returned to profitability sequentially, compared with a net loss of ₹4.1 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue rose 33.6% to ₹767.8 Cr from ₹574.7 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, it increased 12.3% from ₹683.8 Cr.

Including other income and finance income, total income stood at ₹786.4 Cr. Total expenses increased 32.4% to ₹766.9 Cr from ₹579 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

Separately, WeWork India reported an IGAAP-equivalent net profit of ₹65.8 Cr, up 67.4% from ₹39.3 Cr a year earlier. Total revenue on this basis increased 31.6% to ₹768.7 Cr.

The company’s IGAAP-equivalent presentation adjusts the treatment of leases and certain other items under Ind AS. These figures differ from its statutory financial results.

On the same basis, EBITDA increased 37.6% to ₹162.9 Cr, with its margin expanding to 21.2% from 20.3% a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA grew 17.8%.

Record Desk Additions

WeWork India added 11,700 desks during the quarter, its largest quarterly addition to date, taking operational capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres in eight cities. Capacity increased 26.9% from a year earlier.

The company added 18,400 desks in the first half of FY27, with another approximately 4,500 desks becoming operational in the first week of October.

In his letter to shareholders, MD and CEO Karan Virwani said the bulk of the company’s ongoing capital expenditure cycle was now operational. He expects these centres to support operating leverage as they mature.

WeWork India’s expansion pipeline comprises more than 9,000 desks under signed leases and over 38,000 desks covered by letters of intent (LOIs). Including these, the company pegged its total planned capacity at 1,90,000-1,95,000 desks.

Its member base increased 32.5% to 1,21,700, outpacing capacity growth. Portfolio occupancy stood at 83.7%, up 357 basis points (bps) from a year earlier.

However, occupancy declined 114 bps sequentially, which the company attributed to newly added capacity that was still being filled.

Global capability centres contributed 40.8% of core revenue during the quarter.

Services Outpace Core Growth

Beyond its core private office and managed office offerings, WeWork India earns revenue from value-added services (VAS), including events, food and beverages, office customisation, and technology services. Its digital offerings include on-demand workspace access and virtual offices.

On an IGAAP-equivalent basis, combined VAS and digital revenue grew 38% to ₹108.8 Cr, outpacing the 31.7% increase in core revenue to ₹657.7 Cr.

VAS revenue rose 35.2% to ₹79.6 Cr, while digital revenue increased 45.6% to ₹29.2 Cr.

The company’s contracted core revenue stood at ₹3,843 Cr, up 66% from a year earlier, against corresponding committed rent of ₹1,421 Cr.

WeWork India reported a net cash position of ₹23.1 Cr at the end of September as against a net debt of ₹310.5 Cr a year earlier.
